name: DLL Search Order Hijacking

evidence.rationale: Unauthorized DLLs fail to load if not on the allowlist, directly mitigating search order hijacking. Side-loaded malicious libraries are blocked when load validation is enforced.

Applying vendor patches to vulnerable applications can correct unsafe DLL search paths, missing library references, and other side-loading conditions that allow an adversary-controlled DLL to execute. It does not prevent DLL hijacking in unpatched software or through writable application directories.

Vendor patches can correct unsafe DLL search paths, missing library references, and other side-loading conditions that allow an adversary-controlled DLL to execute. This does not prevent DLL hijacking in unsupported software.
Applying secure design principles to include hash values in manifest files, where possible, can help prevent adversaries from side-loading malicious dynamic-link library (DLL) files.
Use vetted platform and application security modules to validate component integrity; where applicable, include hash values in manifest files to help prevent malicious DLL side-loading.

Static and build-time checks can identify insecure DLL search behavior and verify expected library paths or manifest integrity information, reducing opportunities for malicious DLL side-loading or search-order hijacking in developed applications.
